scenes.text: Sloths only poop about once a week, and they risk their lives to do it.
They spend almost their whole life upside down in the treetops.
They eat, sleep, mate and even give birth upside down.
Their leafy diet has few calories, so they move very slowly.
A sloth may travel only about forty yards in a whole day.
Their metabolism runs at less than half the normal rate for an animal their size.
Digesting one meal can take days, among the slowest of any mammal.
So, about once a week, a three-toed sloth climbs down to the ground.
At the base of its tree it does its business, where predators can catch it.
Scientists think the reason might involve tiny moths that live in sloth fur.
The moths lay their eggs in the dung, and the new moths fly up to find a sloth.
They help fertilize green algae growing in the sloth's fur.
That algae helps camouflage the sloth, which may even eat it for energy.
Oh, and these slowpokes are surprisingly good swimmers.
Would you risk your life for a bathroom break?

title: Sloths risk their lives to poop once a week 🦥
caption: Sloths live upside down in the trees but climb down about once a week to poop, where predators can catch them. Scientists think tiny moths and algae in their fur may explain why.
